# `scss/dollar-variable-pattern`

**`$variables` are kebab-case**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Pack** | `@codelaw/rules-scss` (npm) · `codelaw-rules-scss` (PyPI) |
| **Languages** | SCSS |
| **Turned on by** | `codelaw:scss/strict` at `error` |
| **Severity when named without one** | `error` |
| **Options** | `pattern` |
| **Fix** | `auto` — `codelaw fix` applies it; it never changes what the code does (auto when every file that uses the variable reaches it through `@use`, `@forward` or `@import`: the rename then changes every use, as one fix; a user that reaches it another way makes the rename a diff to accept, and another file declaring the same name offers none (SR-MULTI-FILE-FIXES)) |
| **Stability** | `preview` — runs only with `preview = true` |
| **Since** | 0.3.0 |
| **Ported from** | `stylelint-scss/dollar-variable-pattern` |

## What it checks

`$variable` names match a pattern, kebab-case by default.

**Why:** A consistent scheme makes names predictable across a codebase.

## Configuration

Everything below goes in `codelaw.toml` at the repo root. The same keys work as `[tool.codelaw]` in `pyproject.toml` or `"codelaw"` in `package.json` ([SR-CONFIG](../../../records/0110_config.md)).

### Turn it on

**Install the pack** (`codelaw init` does it for the languages it finds):

```bash
npm install --save-dev @codelaw/rules-scss
pip install codelaw-rules-scss
```

**Then extend a preset that turns it on** — `codelaw:scss/strict` sets it to `error`:

```toml
preview = true                        # pack rules are preview today
extends = ["codelaw:scss/strict"]
```

- **A rule exists only once its pack is loaded** through `extends`; naming it in `[rules]` without that is an unknown rule id (exit 2).
- **Without `preview = true`** the rule is skipped and codelaw warns that it is preview.

### Severity

```toml
[rules]
"scss/dollar-variable-pattern" = "warn"    # error | warn | info | off
```

- **`error`** fails the run (exit 1) · **`warn`** fails only with `--max-warnings N` · **`info`** never fails · **`off`** turns it off.
- **Naming it with a severity turns it on** even when no preset does.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pattern` | `string` | `"^[a-z][a-z0-9]*(-[a-z0-9]+)*$"` | a regular expression the name, without its `$`, must match |

**Every option at its default** — a starting point to copy:

```toml
[rules."scss/dollar-variable-pattern"]
severity = "error"

[rules."scss/dollar-variable-pattern".options]
pattern = "^[a-z][a-z0-9]*(-[a-z0-9]+)*$"
```

**The same, inline, with example values:**

```toml
[rules]
"scss/dollar-variable-pattern" = { severity = "error", options = { pattern = "^[a-z][a-z0-9]*(-[a-z0-9]+)*$" } }
```

- **A table without `severity`** changes only the options: the severity stays what a preset or an earlier layer set, and a rule that is off stays off.
- **A list option replaces its default** — copy the default entries you want to keep.
- **An unknown option or a value of the wrong type** stops the run with exit 2 and names the nearest option.

#### `pattern`

*string* · default `"^[a-z][a-z0-9]*(-[a-z0-9]+)*$"`

a regular expression the name, without its `$`, must match

```toml
[rules."scss/dollar-variable-pattern".options]
pattern = "^[a-z][a-z0-9]*(-[a-z0-9]+)*$"
```

### For a group of files

A `[scope.<name>]` gives some files their own setting, applied after `[rules]` — a scope of your own needs `files`:

```toml
[scope.legacy]
files = ["src/legacy/**/*.scss"]
rules = { "scss/dollar-variable-pattern" = { options = { pattern = "^[a-z][a-z0-9]*(-[a-z0-9]+)*$" } } }
```

Or switch it off there:

```toml
[scope.legacy]
files = ["src/legacy/**/*.scss"]
rules = { "scss/dollar-variable-pattern" = "off" }
```

A scope's `remap` changes whole severities in its files, after everything else: `remap = { error = "warn" }` never fails the run there.

### Warn locally, fail in CI

The `ci` profile runs when `CI` is set; `local` otherwise; `--profile <name>` or `CODELAW_PROFILE` picks one.

```toml
[profile.local.rules]
"scss/dollar-variable-pattern" = "warn"

[profile.ci.rules]
"scss/dollar-variable-pattern" = "error"
```

### In `pyproject.toml` or `package.json`

```toml
# pyproject.toml
[tool.codelaw.rules]
"scss/dollar-variable-pattern" = { severity = "warn", options = { pattern = "^[a-z][a-z0-9]*(-[a-z0-9]+)*$" } }
```

```json
{
  "codelaw": {
    "rules": {
      "scss/dollar-variable-pattern": {"severity": "warn", "options": {"pattern": "^[a-z][a-z0-9]*(-[a-z0-9]+)*$"}}
    }
  }
}
```

### Silence one finding

An inline `codelaw-ignore` always needs a reason; `expires=`, `warn_days=` and `by=` date it ([SR-LINTER](../../../records/0106_linter.md) decision 6).

- **SCSS:** `// codelaw-ignore scss/dollar-variable-pattern: <reason>`
- **Dated:** `// codelaw-ignore scss/dollar-variable-pattern expires=2026-12-31 by=you@example.com: <reason>`

### Keep today's findings, fail on new ones

```bash
codelaw baseline add --rule scss/dollar-variable-pattern --expires 2026-12-31 --reason "<why>"
```

See [SR-BASELINE](../../../records/0104_baseline-and-deprecations.md).

### See what applies

```bash
codelaw explain scss/dollar-variable-pattern       # what it wants, why, how to fix
codelaw check --rule scss/dollar-variable-pattern  # only this rule
codelaw config --print --for <file>                # the resolved setting, and where it came from
```

## How to fix

1. `codelaw fix` renames the variable to kebab-case here and in every file that uses it.
2. Where the rename is a suggestion (a user reaches the file some other way), check the diff and accept it with `codelaw fix --unsafe`.
3. A pattern that isn't kebab-case, or a new name already taken, offers no rename: rename it and every use by hand.

## Examples

### SCSS

#### Don't

```scss
$FontSize: 16px;
```

#### Do

```scss
$font-size: 16px;
```

#### Don't

```scss
// src/_tokens.scss
$FontSize: 16px;
// src/app.scss
@use "tokens";
.a {
  font-size: tokens.$FontSize;
}
```

#### Do

```scss
// src/_tokens.scss
$font-size: 16px;
// src/app.scss
@use "tokens";
.a {
  font-size: tokens.$font-size;
}
```

## Differences from the source

The pattern applies to declarations, not to the names in an `@each` or a mixin's parameter list.
